identity.real_world_identity_notes: McLaren MP4/7A, the Honda RA122E/B V12 car of 1992 and the first McLaren with a semi-automatic transmission: a McLaren transverse six-speed with an electro-hydraulic clutch and paddle shift that let the driver hold the throttle while the system changed gear.

wheel_rim.notes: Observed from the cockpit during the guided drive.

notes: Simulator behaviour was directly observed in a guided drive in AMS2 1.6.9.91 with automatic clutch and shifting disabled: automatic cut and blip, and the car pulled away without a clutch.
The electro-hydraulic clutch is why no driver clutch is needed to pull away, unlike the Gen1 cars in the same class, which is recorded rather than smoothed over.

Clutch telemetry was present while the running shifts were accepted as clutchless. The channel cannot separate the pedal from the clutch the car works itself, and this gearbox works its own on every shift, so the accepted results stand. The driver confirmed no pedal was used.

Only the high-downforce identity was observed. AMS2 selects the aero configuration from the circuit, so this car reports a different identity at a low-downforce track; that identity is not recorded here because it has not been observed and an exact match cannot be guessed.
Observed live in AMS2 1.6.9.91 via guided verification observation ams2.mclaren-honda-mp4-7a-high-downforce.20260814t223806640z-12e37430 by Jason Kinslow.

confidence.basis: Simulator behaviour was live-tested in AMS2 1.6.9.91 with automatic clutch and shifting disabled, and the real-world transmission is supported by registered sources.

claims.basis: A registered source establishes the MP4/7A and its transmission, and the exact simulator identity was observed live.

Wikipedia gives a McLaren transverse 6-speed semi-automatic with an electro-hydraulic clutch and paddle shift, and the live drive selected six paddle gears with automatic cut and blip and no clutch needed to pull away.
Directly observed during the guided drive: move-off, shift clutch use, automatic cut and blip, and the cockpit rim.
